subject: POC Infrastructure Runbook — MAP next steps & owners
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Paul Nguyen <paul.nguyen@acme.com>
Cc: Sarah Li <sli@acme.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 1 Nov 2026 15:15:00 -0700
Subject: POC Infrastructure Runbook — MAP next steps & owners

Hi Paul / Sarah —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Per our discussion attached is a first-pass runbook (MAP milestone table) focused on the POC environment dependencies we agreed are blockers for the initial test—VPC peering, IP allowlists, SSO/SAML, and secrets/KMS. I pulled together proposed owners and target dates so we can lock the pilot window.

Top-level asks / assumptions:
- Redwood will provide a read-only test service account and the egress IP range for allowlist (we can provide an updated list after initial traffic profiling).
- Acme will create the VPC peering connection or accept our peering request in your cloud console.
- SSO: we'd like SAML metadata from your IdP; if you want us to initiate, send the ACS/Entity ID we should use.
- Secrets: prefer customer-managed KMS keys for secrets in the POC; we can fall back to Redwood-managed if procurement blocks it.

Proposed milestone & owners (see attached spreadsheet for row-level detail):
1) Confirm VPC peer + routing (Owner: Acme - Paul) — target: 2026-11-10
2) IP allowlist + firewall rules (Owner: Acme - Paul) — target: 2026-11-12
3) SSO/SAML exchange & test user (Owner: Acme - Sarah / Redwood - Jordan) — target: 2026-11-15
4) Secrets/KMS access & service account (Owner: Acme - Security / Redwood infra) — target: 2026-11-15
5) Smoke test + validation (Owner: Redwood / Acme) — target: 2026-11-18

Next steps I suggest:
- Paul: accept the peering request or confirm preferred window for us to create it (we typically need a 1-hour maintenance window).
- Sarah: share SAML metadata and indicate whether test users can be provisioned in your IdP.
- Marissa (cc'd): I'll loop in Solutions Engineering for the smoke-test runbook once network and SSO are green.

Attachments: MAP-poc-infra-runbook-v1.xlsx (milestone table), acme-network-diagram.png (reference)

If these target dates look tight, tell me which ones we should slide — our goal is to start the POC by the week of Nov 22, but we can shift the pilot start if your team needs more runway.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0134

--

From: Paul Nguyen <paul.nguyen@acme.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sarah Li <sli@acme.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 09:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: POC Infrastructure Runbook — MAP next steps & owners

Jordan —

Appreciate the clear runbook. A few notes from infra/security:

- VPC peering: we prefer to have Acme initiate the peering request (security policy). I'll schedule the peering for 2026-11-09 at 10:00 PST. Please confirm the exact CIDR we'll peer to and whether we need BGP or static routing.
- IP allowlist: we can open a single /29 for the POC egress; want to confirm the IPs you expect and whether additional ranges are likely during heavy tokenization tests.
- KMS: security policy requires customer-managed keys for dev only if the POC contains customer data. For the initial test we'll use a restricted Redwood-managed key; if we move to production we will provision an Acme KMS key.
- SSO: Sarah will share SAML metadata. We prefer that Redwood acts as SP and Acme as IdP. Test user provisioning is fine.

Attachments: acme-current-firewall-rules.pdf (reference)

I'll loop in our cloud partner (Tom Elliott) if we run into peering routing edge cases.

Thanks —
Paul
Senior Cloud Engineer | Acme Corporation
paul.nguyen@acme.com

On Sun, Nov 1, 2026 at 3:15 PM Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com> wrote:
> [original message truncated]

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Paul Nguyen <paul.nguyen@acme.com>
Cc: Sarah Li <sli@acme.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC Infrastructure Runbook — MAP next steps & owners

Paul — thanks, that's super helpful. Answers inline and a couple clarifications: 

- CIDR: we'll peer to 10.48.0.0/16 from the Redwood side for the test environment (no BGP needed; static routes are fine for this POC). If you prefer a smaller range we can shrink it to a /20.
- IP allowlist: initial /29 works. I'll confirm the exact egress addresses after our perf run; worst-case we may need to add a second /29 but we'll run with one to start.
- KMS: understood — use Redwood-managed restricted key for the POC. We'll provide an alternative flow if you want to test customer-managed later in the pilot.
- SAML/SP configuration: Redwood will be SP. I'll send the SP metadata and an ACS URL by end of day.

Operational note for smoke test: Marissa will lead the test script creation (connectivity, token exchange, small inference batch). Marissa — can you prepare a 20-minute checklist we can run jointly once SSO and network are confirmed? Preferably something automatable we can run from our pipeline.

If everyone is OK with the dates Paul proposed I'll update the MAP spreadsheet and send a revised row-level timeline by EOD.

Thanks,
Jordan

From: Sarah Li <sli@acme.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>, Paul Nguyen <paul.nguyen@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC Infrastructure Runbook — MAP next steps & owners

Jordan / Paul / Marissa —

Quick update from security/identity:
- SAML metadata attached to this thread (saml-metadata-acme.xml). We'll create a test group "redwood-poc" and add two test users by close of business 2026-11-04.
- Approved the use of a Redwood-managed restricted key for the initial POC. If we extend to customer data we will require Acme KMS.
- Peering window confirmed for 2026-11-09 starting 10:00 PST. Paul will post the peering request in our ticket system and tag Redwood for approval.

Marissa: please coordinate the test script with our identity team once the test users are available.

I'll mark the SSO milestone as in-progress; expect metadata delivered as a Drive link in a follow-up.

Thanks,
Sarah Li
Director, Security & Identity | Acme Corporation
